title: Changelog - November 19, 2026
summary: This week's Corgea changelog expands finding exports, adds more control to the findings API, and keeps long-running reports moving in the background.
body_markdown:
This week’s roundup covers public Corgea releases from November 13 through November 17, 2026. The updates make it easier to export findings across categories, filter findings through the API, and retrieve reports when they are ready.


## Top 3 features


### 1. Export several finding types together


You can now export several finding types in one CSV from the Workbench, or combine supported scan finding types in one CSV, SARIF, or PDF report. Choose the types before reviewing their shared filters, then revise the selection with **Change types** if needed.


Large CSV exports arrive as ZIP files with an export-criteria summary. The dialog asks you to acknowledge that the file contains sensitive vulnerability data, and an email links to the completed download. Learn more about[finding exports](https://docs.corgea.app/issue_export) .


### 2. Filter findings by auto-triage result or scan


The findings API now returns auto-triage verdicts and supports` auto_triage


`


and` scan_id


`


filters. The` auto_triage


`


filter lets integrations request findings whose newest detection was marked` false_positive


`


or` valid


`


, while` scan_id


`


returns each matching finding once for a specified scan.


Status filtering now matches the Workbench, and unknown query parameters return an error instead of an unfiltered list. The[findings API reference](https://docs.corgea.app/api-reference/findings/list-findings) has the full parameter and response details.


### 3. Let PDF reports and exports finish in the background


Scan PDF reports now keep building after you close the dialog. When the report is ready, find it in Recent exports and download it there. Longer-running exports show progress, rows exported, and estimated time remaining. You can reopen their progress from Recent exports, and Corgea emails a download link for exports that take longer to finish.


Download links now expire 12 hours after completion. If an export expires, you can rebuild it with the same criteria and current findings.


## More features and improvements


- SAML group mapping patterns now support` {NUMERIC_ID}


`


, so one role mapping can match numbered groups while keeping a separate team for each group.
- You can sort the Scans list by date, status, or project name. The selection stays in place while you browse, filter, and refresh.
- Project Tag and Team filters, plus Tag filters in Scans, Workbench, Workbench exports, and Dependencies, now load options as you search for more responsive large lists.
- Export dialogs show finding types hidden behind the “+N more” badge in a tooltip on hover or keyboard focus.
- Finding CSVs put Finding Type second, use consistent type labels, and no longer include Fix Status or Scan Metadata.
- Large Workbench exports count findings progressively to keep the dialog responsive.
- Interrupted background exports retry once automatically, and temporary file-delivery failures retry without rebuilding the export.
- Scan histories load faster, show links to the first and last pages, and cap totals at 10,000+. Scans with multiple scheduled runs no longer appear more than once.
- Code quality findings now follow the PR rule’s Severity setting. Each PR scan adds at most six new code quality comments without letting non-commentable findings use the limit.
- Confirmation prompts now use the in-app dialog, with improved keyboard focus when dialogs overlap.
- Pull request creation shows a clear error when Azure DevOps, Bitbucket, or Harness refuses the request.
- The projects list no longer fails to load when a repository URL has no organization segment.
